feat(mini): publish Zod Mini as the standalone @zod/mini package (#6491)

* feat(mini): publish Zod Mini as the standalone @zod/mini package

A new packages/mini workspace package re-exports zod/mini with zod as a peer dependency, built with zshy's single types condition. Its version and peer floor are kept in lockstep with zod by check-versions.ts, release.yml publishes it after zod, and the resolution and integration suites cover its built types.

* fix(mini): publish @zod/mini last and skip its version check on prereleases

Review follow-up on #6491: the mini publish now runs after zod's tag, GitHub release and JSR publish so a failed mini publish cannot strand a published zod; check-versions.ts only enforces the mini lockstep on latest and refuses a prerelease publish of @zod/mini; the .cts/.mts resolution fixtures import @zod/mini; the release procedure in AGENTS.md lists the fourth file; funding block parity.

* docs: count four files in the release procedure comment

* ci: sync @zod/mini to 4.5.3 and add a workflow_dispatch back-publish for the scoped package

The dispatch input publishes @zod/mini alone at an x.y.z that zod already shipped, with the peer floor set to that minor and the lockstep check skipped, so 4.5.0 through 4.5.2 can be published with provenance under the same trusted publisher.

* ci: back-publish @zod/mini under a backfill dist-tag

npm refuses a bare publish of a version below latest, so the dispatch job tags it backfill and the release docs say

build(deps): upgrade eslint to v10 (#7576)

Layer 5 of a stacked dependency upgrade. Stacked on #7575.

| package | from | to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eslint` | ^9.26.0 | **^10.10.0** |
| `typescript-eslint` | ^8.32 | ^8.70.0 |
| `eslint-plugin-unicorn` | 64.0.0 | ^74.0.0 |
| `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` | **6.0.0-rc.1** | ^7.1.1 |
| `@eslint/compat` | ^2.0.0 | ^2.1.1 |

`eslint-plugin-react` stays at 7.37.5 — there's no newer release. Note
this also gets us off a release-candidate prerelease of
`eslint-plugin-react-hooks`.

### Config migration
- **`reactHooks.configs.recommended` is eslintrc-shaped again in v7**
and makes ESLint 10 fail outright (`A config object has a "plugins" key
defined as an array of strings`). The flat config moved to
`configs.flat.recommended`. Same fix applied to the two example configs
that wire this up themselves.
- **`react-hooks/react-compiler` no longer exists.** v7 split it into
~14 granular rules (`purity`, `immutability`, `refs`,
`set-state-in-effect`, `use-memo`, …) that `flat.recommended` enables.
The rule entry and two stale `eslint-disable` comments referencing it
are removed.
- **`unicorn/filename-case` gets `checkDirectories: false`.** unicorn 74
started checking directory names and flagged deliberate ones
(`__tests__`, `aws-lambda`, `node-http`, `app-dir`). This keeps the rule
scoped to filenames, as before.
- **`max-params` now counts parameters of function _types_.** The single
hit is `setQueriesData`, which mirrors TanStack Query's

## 🎯 Changes

What changes are made in this PR? Is it a feature or a bug fix?

Adds a TypeScript-compiler-driven OpenAPI 3.1 document generator to
@trpc/openapi. The generator resolves fully-computed types (what the
vanilla client proxy sees) rather than raw mapped/generic types, and
emits a standards-compliant JSON spec, possible for use with any
generator or consumer of such a document

This diff is big and it mostly doesn't matter because it's testing code
which you can ignore!

Focus on:

* packages/openapi/src/generate.ts
* packages/openapi/test/generate.test.ts
* examples/openapi-codegen (based on the minimal example)
* The versions script has been updating to publish this package as
`11.12.0-alpha` and update the version number of releases

## Summary

Follow-up to merged #99086, addressing [bgw’s Jest transformer
review](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/99086#discussion_r4100921785)
and the remaining GitHub API rate-limit concern. The gate still waits
for **any of the nearest three PRs** to pass its required check, failing
closed if all three fail. Fork, leaf and first-three PR behavior is
unchanged.

- Refresh the current PR / branch-link topology every **20 minutes**
while waiting; on each intervening **five-minute** poll, fetch only the
up-to-three predecessor check statuses. Revalidate live PR revisions and
checks before *any* success/failure decision. A changed decisive
snapshot triggers an immediate topology refresh; repeated invalidation
backs off.
- Replace the bespoke TypeScript Jest transformer with `ts-jest`, using
the action’s local pinned Jest 29 runner and peers. Keep independent
`tsc --noEmit` typechecking and TypeScript 6.0.2. Refresh the compiled
action and fake-timer tests.

### REST request rate per steadily waiting middle PR

| Poll | Previous | New |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First poll and every 20 minutes | 8 | 8 (topology + up to 3 checks) |
| 5/10/15 minutes between topology refreshes | 8 each | 3 each (checks
only) |
| **20-minute total** | **32** | **17** |
| **Steady-state hourly rate** | **96/hour** | **51/hour (~47% fewer)**
|

turbopack-ecmascript-runtime: type-check every runtime file (#99670)

## Summary

Most of the Turbopack runtime in `turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/src`
was never type-checked, and editors showed hundreds of bogus "Cannot
find name" errors in it.

- `src/nodejs/tsconfig.json` had `"include": ["*.ts"]`, which only
matched `nodejs/hmr-types.d.ts`. So `nodejs/runtime/*` and
`nodejs/dev/*` were in no project, and `pnpm check` never covered them.
- `browser/runtime/base/tsconfig.json` included only `runtime-base.ts`
and `dummy.ts`. `build-base.ts`, `dev-base.ts` and `dev-dummy.ts` were
left out. `dev-base.ts` was checked indirectly through the `dom`
project.
- tsserver then fell back to `turbopack/tsconfig.json`, which uses
`"module": "NodeNext"`. That implies `moduleDetection: force`, so these
global-script files were treated as modules and their shared `///
<reference>` declarations disappeared.

`build-base.ts` and `dev-base.ts` are alternative entry points that both
define `instantiateModule`, so they can't share a project. In both
`nodejs/` and `browser/runtime/base/`, `tsconfig.json` is now a
solution-style config that references a `tsconfig.build.json` and a
`tsconfig.dev.json`. tsserver follows these references, so every file
opens in the right project. Files that are only pulled in through `///
<reference>` are listed in `include` explicitly, because tsserver
doesn't otherwise count them as part of a project. The `check:` scripts
are split the same way.

Turbopack: Reorganize runtime files into shared/runtime directory (#89461)

This change moves runtime code that does not use a module system and is concatenated by Rust into a dedicated `runtime/` directory so it's not confused with other code. 

It also codifies this in a README and instructs agents to read nearby READMEs so they enforce this convention.

**This change only moves code and does not refactor any further.** Snapshot updates reflect the new file paths in the generated runtime code.

**Test Plan:** CI, existing tests
